newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares recover, advances seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares recover, advances seen continuing.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Friday in a modest recovery with dealers seeing gains early next week if nothing untoward happened on Wall Street.

"The market counter-reacted today after Thursday's plunge. Provided nothing unexpected happens we could see modest gains on Monday, when the focus will again be on companies announcing 1996 corporate results," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 0.24 point up at 153.99, while the June KFX future slipped 3.90 point to 153.60 with only five contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Dealers said activity next week would be focused around FOMC, with investors cautious ahead of the Tuesday meeting.
Many key players were expected to be away from the market ahead of the Easter break which starts in Denmark on Wednesday night.

FLS Industries closed five crowns up at 815 ahead of its 1996 result expected next week. Novo Nordisk shed seven to close at 683, leading banks posted small gains, led by Unidanmark, which put on six crowns to end the week at 346.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.956 billion crowns.
